findings.headline: 70.0% of daily departures are compressed into 5 rush hours
findings.details: Out of 100 scheduled daily trips, 70 depart during morning ([8, 9]) and evening ([17, 18, 19]) peak hours. Off-peak service drops from 14.0 trips/hr to 1.6 trips/hr.
findings.business_implication: Timetables reflect severe rush-hour supply compression. Midday and evening off-peak commuters experience extended headways despite active fleet allocations.

findings.headline: Top 5 interchange hubs carry 50.0% of all corridor transfer connections
findings.details: The top 5 multi-route interchanges handle 30 of 60 route-stop transfer opportunities across 30 physical bus stops.
findings.business_implication: The transit network exhibits hub-and-spoke interchange vulnerability. Infrastructure disruptions or terminal bottlenecks at super-hubs propagate network-wide cascading delays.

findings.headline: 20.0% of corridors shut down completely on weekends
findings.details: 2 lines operate Monday through Friday with zero Saturday or Sunday trips scheduled, leaving cross-town transit corridors unserved.
findings.business_implication: Weekend retail, hospital, and service-sector mobility is structurally unserved on key arterial lines, creating immediate farebox revenue recapture opportunities via idle-depot weekend rosters.

findings.headline: 100.0% of corridors operate with off-peak intervals >= 270 minutes
findings.details: Because trips are clustered in peak hours, 10 of 10 corridors run <=2 trips across the remaining 19 off-peak operating hours.
findings.business_implication: Off-peak service behaves as sporadic single-run scheduled dispatch rather than true frequent-network transit, severely limiting non-commute utility.

findings.headline: Flat corridor trip allocation fails to reflect network transfer demand
findings.details: Routes receive uniform daily allocations regardless of whether they serve 7 transfer connections or 18 transfer connections, indicating legacy scheduling rather than supply optimization.
findings.business_implication: High-degree arterial corridors are under-supplied relative to their network connectivity, while peripheral feeder lines absorb equivalent bus assets.

findings.headline: Regional holiday surges project +260 (base) to +420 (high) supplemental runs
findings.details: Multi-scenario modeling based on regional holiday calendars indicates fleet surge requirements concentrating at major interchange terminals.
findings.business_implication: Without contingency scheduling and maintenance-window optimization, peak holiday travel periods overwhelm terminus infrastructure and bus availability.
